title: Water model diagram sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 34 (Water model diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 34: Models for circuits. To understand how models help explain what happens in a circuit and where they break down

picture.draw: Draw and label: Water model diagram sheet

questions.q: In the water model, what does a narrow pipe represent?
questions.model: What does a narrow pipe do? Slows the water. What slows current? Resistance. So the narrow pipe is a resistance.

questions.q: Why is current the same all round the loop in the rope model?
questions.a: The rope moves at the same speed everywhere

questions.q: Give one weakness of the rope model.
questions.a: For example: it does not show energy being carried from cell to lamp well

questions.q: Draw the water model of a series circuit with one cell and two lamps. Label each part with the circuit word.
questions.a: Pump labelled cell, pipes wires, two narrow sections lamps, arrows for flow
questions.model: Teacher draws the pump and labels it 'cell: pushes the current'.

questions.q: Evaluate the water model in the portal response box: one strength, one weakness. Starter: 'The model is useful because...'
questions.a: Strength: shows current is not used up; weakness: a cut pipe leaks but a cut wire just stops.

questions.q: Invent your own model (for example a train track) and match all five parts.
questions.a: Pupils' own, each part matched correctly
A simpler way to picture something
options: A simpler way to picture something

questions.q: Big question: how would you explain a circuit to a Year 5?
questions.a: With a model such as water in pipes: pump is the cell, flow is the current.
